transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-06-10 16:00 PDT
- Duration: 42 minutes (approx)
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Mei (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Aisha (CTO), Tom (Head of Security), Diego (ML Eng), Sofia (Platform)

Summary (auto):
Customer evaluating Redwood for a 6-week pilot focused on LLM inference for fraud-detection scoring and customer support summarization. Primary constraints: SOC 2 / ISO compliance, SSO via SAML, strict RBAC and audit logging, key management and data residency. Discussed workload sizing for benchmarks, success criteria (latency P95, token cost, model quality), and pilot timelines. Agreed action items and next steps.

Topics: pilot success criteria, workload shapes and sizing, benchmark plan, security/compliance for pilot (SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs), private vs dedicated deployment tradeoffs, KMS/HSM, auditability.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick audio check?
[00:03] Aisha: Good here.
[00:05] Tom: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:10] Jordan: Great. Quick intro, I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, Mei is our inference SE, Ravi's on for infra questions. We're excited to scope the pilot. Maybe start with you Aisha to frame goals?
[00:22] Aisha: Sure. We're looking at two initial production use cases — a real-time fraud scoring model that needs low latency and a batch summarization pipeline for customer support transcripts. The pilot goal is to validate latency/cost and compliance controls. Need to know if Redwood can meet SOC 2 requirements and integrate with our SSO and audit tooling.
[00:38] Mei: Makes sense. Can you share current throughput numbers and token lengths for those flows?
[00:44] Diego: Yeah for fraud scoring, average prompt is short, 60 to 120 tokens, P95 latency target is sub-120ms for inference path — that's pretty aggressive. We expect bursts up to 250 concurrent requests, sustained maybe 50 qps. For summarization, batch jobs are 10k to 50k transcripts per day, sequences up to 1,500 tokens, latency tolerant to minutes.
[01:10] Jordan: Good detail, thanks. On the security side Tom, what are your must-haves for the pilot?
[01:15] Tom: Must-haves are SOC 2 Type II evidence, SAML-based SSO into our Okta, RBAC that lets us partition environments per business unit, immutable audit logs with export, and customer-managed KMS/HSM would be preferred. Data residency in GCP europe-west if possible. Also need to confirm retention and deletion controls.
[01:37] Mei: Quick clarifying Q — when you say customer-managed KMS, do you mean Redwood bringing a VPC connector and using your Google KMS, or a bring-your-own-hsm approach?
[01:46] Tom: Ideally BYOK via customer KMS integration; if that's not possible for the pilot we'd accept a solution where keys are controlled by us and we can rotate them.
[01:55] Ravi: We support Cloud KMS integrations for Private deployments and we have a key wrap approach for dedicated as well. For hosted we can discuss envelope encryption patterns. We'll capture details in docs.
[02:06] Aisha: Timeline-wise we want the pilot to start mid-June and run 6 weeks with the first benchmark run in week 1 to validate throughput and cost.
[02:16] Jordan: That aligns. Our typical pilot has an initial discovery/ingestion week, a benchmarking window, and a two-week integration/validation window.
[02:23] Diego: For the benchmark, what artifacts do you need from us?
[02:26] Mei: Ideally you provide a 48-hour traffic trace or a synthetic generator that mirrors bursts, plus representative prompt examples and expected output quality metrics. We'll define a scoring harness — e.g., ROUGE or custom heuristics for summarization and business-rule checks for fraud scoring.
[02:41] Diego: We can extract a sanitized trace; need to confirm PII scrub rules.
[02:45] Tom: Please make sure anything sent to vendor is sanitized or in a secure S3 with limited access.
[02:51] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll accept sanitized samples and can also run on-prem tests if needed.
[02:56] Aisha: On SSO, our security ops requires SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning for users and groups. Any experience?
[03:04] Mei: Yes, we integrate SAML and SCIM; we can map groups to RBAC roles. There are some product nuances — for dedicated and private we can do deeper mapping, for hosted there are OOTB mappings. We'll share SAML configuration docs.
[03:18] Tom: Audit logs — we need immutable logs with user, action, timestamp, resource, and an exportable format to our SIEM (Splunk). Retention 1 year minimal.
[03:29] Ravi: We emit structured audit events to a configurable sink and can push to customer SIEM via secure connectors. Retention and immutability depend on deployment mode, but for Private we can guarantee retained logs in your VPC.
[03:41] Aisha: Does Redwood have SOC 2 and ISO certs?
[03:44] Jordan: Yes, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 — we'll share the attestation and scope doc. We'll also include a recent pen test summary and our ATO-like checklist.
[03:55] Tom: Good. We may need your incident response playbook and contact points for escalation.
[03:59] Jordan: We'll include that in the security pack.
[04:03] Diego: Let's dig into benchmarking specifics — Mei, how do you size the dedicated pool for a 250 concurrent burst?
[04:09] Mei: Two levers — model size/variant and batching/backpressure. For sub-120ms P95 at 60–120 token prompts, you probably want a smaller-latency optimized variant and dedicated GPUs with no noisy neighbors. We'd simulate burst concurrency with steady-state warm KV cache; the hottest path is cold-starts and KV misses. For 250 conc bursts, we might need autoscale headroom plus prewarmed instances — we'll draft an instance plan in the benchmark doc.
[04:41] Diego: Cold-starts are a big concern — what's typical warmup?
[04:44] Mei: With our runtime KV cache and continuous batching, warmup is in the tens of seconds, but the fastest path is to keep models resident in the pool. We'll show numbers from similar customers — with pinned models you can hit sub-100ms for small token lengths.
[04:58] Aisha: Cost target for fraud scoring is $0.0015 per request (roughly) — can you ballpark tokens per request and cost?
[05:06] Jordan: We'll need to run the benchmark but rough math: at 80 tokens per request, that's ~80 input tokens plus maybe 10 output. We'll propose model quantization and batching tradeoffs; Redwood Optimize will recommend a profile. We'll include a cost projection in the plan.
[05:21] Tom: For compliance, we need to ensure data in transit and at rest are encrypted with customer keys, and that logs can't be tampered with. Also, role separation for dev/test/prod so devs can't access production prompts.
[05:34] Ravi: RBAC models support resource-level permissions; for private deployments we can integrate with your LDAP via SCIM and map OU groups to role bindings.
[05:43] Diego: Any limitations around private model hosting or bringing our own model?
[05:47] Mei: You can bring your own weights in Private; we have onboarding steps for model vetting and runtime optimization. For hosted, we usually host open models or verified variants, but we can run a pilot in a dedicated sandbox too.
[05:59] Aisha: About audit logs again — do you provide Append-only logs? We need tamper evidence.
[06:04] Ravi: We can use write-once log sinks in Private deployments and support object immutability policies. For hosted we'll provide signed audit records and export hooks; we'll share specifics in the security pack.
[06:15] Tom: Are there cross-region data flows? We need data residency in EU.
[06:20] Jordan: We have GCP europe-west and can pin pilot workloads to that region. We'll confirm networking egress rules.
[06:28] Diego: For the benchmark harness, can Redwood run latency and quality side-by-side across quantized models to show tradeoffs?
[06:34] Mei: Yes — we'll run the same workload across model variants and provide per-route token cost, latency P50/P95/P99, and quality metrics. We'll also include failure modes and fallbacks (e.g., degrade to a smaller model on capacity pressure).
[06:48] Aisha: On SSO provisioning, we need SCIM to create service accounts with constrained roles for the pilot.
[06:54] Jordan: SCIM provisioning is supported; we'll include a sample mapping file.
[06:58] Tom: Regarding IR and SLA — for the pilot we still want a 99.5% availability target and an escalation path.
[07:06] Jordan: Pilot SLAs are typically looser, but we can commit to operational targets and a documented escalation path. If the pilot converts, we'll include SLA language in the contract.
[07:15] Diego: Any limitations on redaction or PII scrubbing within Redwood pipeline?
[07:19] Mei: We provide optional pre-processing hooks to run redaction before tokens hit the model; for Private deployments you can run the scrubber in your VPC.
[07:28] Aisha: Let's talk success criteria concretely — what measurements do you propose?
[07:33] Mei: Proposal: 1) Fraud scoring: P95 latency <= 120ms, sustained throughput 50 qps, burst resilience to 250 conc with <2x latency increase, cost per request <= $0.002. 2) Summarization: Quality score (custom rubric) >= baseline, throughput to process 10k transcripts/day, and output consistency. Also operational criteria: SAML SSO mapped to RBAC, KMS keys used for at-rest encryption, audit logs exported to Splunk.
[08:02] Tom: That looks reasonable; we might tighten the cost target.
[08:06] Jordan: We can iterate after first benchmark.
[08:09] Diego: For benchmarking, will Redwood run it in our account or in Redwood's dedicated pool?
[08:13] Mei: We typically run initial benchmarks in a Redwood dedicated pool (hosted) to prove performance quickly, then replicate in Private/Dedicated in your environment if requested. For the pilot we can do the hosted dedicated pool for the first run, then follow up with a private replication.
[08:27] Sofia: Networking question — will we need VPN or private link for the pilot?
[08:31] Ravi: For Private deployments we use VPC peering or private link; for hosted dedicated we can enable private endpoints. We'll document options and their setup complexity.
[08:40] Aisha: Any data retention defaults? We want to limit storage to 30 days for pilot assets and have purge hooks.
[08:46] Jordan: Retention is configurable — we'll include defaults and show how to configure retention and deletion APIs.
[08:52] Tom: Can you provide a table of controls mapped to SOC 2 criteria?
[08:56] Jordan: Yes — security pack will include a controls matrix mapping to SOC 2 and ISO.
[09:00] Diego: Performance monitoring — is token-level cost breakdown available in console?
[09:04] Mei: Yes, per-route and per-model breakdowns are available with token-level cost and latency heatmaps; we can provide a demo access for the pilot.
[09:12] Aisha: What's the expected total time to get from kickoff to first benchmark? You mentioned week 1 — can you be more specific?
[09:18] Jordan: If we get sanitized samples and SAML configs in 48–72 hours, we can schedule the benchmark on day 5–7. So kickoff mid-June fits.
[09:27] Tom: Any legal requirements for data processing addendum?
[09:30] Jordan: We'll share a DPA, and Redwood supports standard EU data processing addendums.
[09:35] Diego: For model versioning, can we pin a model for the pilot?
[09:39] Mei: Yes, you can pin versions and we can pin the canary to avoid accidental upgrades.
[09:43] Aisha: Okay, let's recap next steps.
[09:46] Jordan: Recap: Redwood to send security pack (SOC2, ISO, pen test summary), SAML/SCIM docs, and initial benchmark plan by 2025-06-12. Customer to provide sanitized dataset and success criteria by 2025-06-13. Schedule private deployment feasibility call week of 2025-06-16.
[10:05] Tom: I'll review the security pack and follow up with specific KMS questions.
[10:09] Diego: I'll get the sanitized samples ready — need clarity on redaction rules, will follow up.
[10:14] Jordan: Great. Any other questions?
[10:16] Aisha: Not from me.
[10:17] Tom: None.
[10:18] Jordan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email and create the pilot ticket in your CRM.
[10:22] Aisha: Thanks all.
